    32	theorem exists_affine_parameters_of_linePoints_subset {K : Type*} [Field K] {m : ℕ}
    33	    (u v u' v' : Fin m → K) (h : linePoints u v ⊆ linePoints u' v') :
    34	    ∃ a b : K, u = u' + a • v' ∧ v = b • v' := by
    35	  obtain ⟨a, ha⟩ := h (show u ∈ linePoints u v from ⟨0, by simp⟩)
    36	  obtain ⟨s, hs⟩ := h (show u + v ∈ linePoints u v from ⟨1, by simp⟩)
    37	  refine ⟨a, s - a, ha, ?_⟩
    38	  calc
    39	    v = (u + v) - u := by abel
    40	    _ = (u' + s • v') - (u' + a • v') := by rw [hs, ha]

    47	theorem exists_isCombineLineCompatible_of_projection_mem {K : Type*} [Field K] {m : ℕ}

   118	`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_subline-claims-line-marginal.tex`. It is not a

   120	theorem not_evaluatesTo_parameter_on_zero_direction {L : LdParams} {c : ℕ}
   121	    (hc : 1 ≤ c) (line : LineDesc L) (hdir : line.direction = 0) :
   122	    ¬ ∃ a : ScalarQ L,
   123	      EvaluatesTo line (Pi.single (⟨1, Nat.lt_succ_of_le hc⟩ : Fin (c + 1)) 1)
   124	        line.base a := by
   125	  have heval (t : ScalarQ L) :
   126	      evalCoefficient (Pi.single (⟨1, Nat.lt_succ_of_le hc⟩ : Fin (c + 1)) 1) t = t := by
   127	    simp [evalCoefficient, Pi.single_apply, ite_mul]
   128	  rintro ⟨a, ha⟩
   129	  have h := (evaluatesTo_zero_direction_iff line hdir _ a).mp ha
   130	  have hzero := h 0
   131	  have hone := h 1
   132	  rw [heval] at hzero hone
   133	  exact zero_ne_one (hzero.trans hone.symm)

    46	def finCombineEquiv (m : ℕ) :

   151	    (hf : f ∈ polyFunc m K d) (hg : g ∈ polyFunc m K d) :
   152	    combinePoly f g ∈ polyFunc (2 * m + 2) K d := by
   153	  have hsymm : Function.Injective (finCombineEquiv m).symm :=
   154	    (finCombineEquiv m).symm.injective
   155	  have hX : Function.Injective (embX m) := by
   156	    intro i j hij
   157	    simpa using hsymm hij
   158	  have hZ : Function.Injective (embZ m) := by
   159	    intro i j hij
   160	    simpa using hsymm hij

   162	    intro i hi
   163	    simpa using hsymm hi
   164	  have haZ : ∀ i, embZ m i ≠ betaVar m := by
   165	    intro i hi
   166	    simpa using hsymm hi

   170	/-- Evaluate one member of a global polynomial pair at a point, selecting the
   171	component by Pauli basis.  This is formalization-only support for
   172	`lem:qld-4-7`, paper
   173	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1267-1274`. -/
   174	def evalAt {P : AdmissibleParams} (W : PauliKind)
   175	    (u : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) (pair : PolyPair P) : PauliScalar P :=
   176	  match W with
   177	  | .X => MvPolynomial.eval u pair.1.1
   178	  | .Z => MvPolynomial.eval u pair.2.1
   179	
   180	/-- The univariate polynomial before coefficient extraction in
   181	`combineLinePoly`.  The four first scalars describe the affine parameters on
   182	the two projected lines; the last four are the affine `alpha` and `beta`
   183	coordinates of the extended line. -/
   184	noncomputable def combineLinePolynomial {K : Type*} [CommSemiring K] {c : ℕ}
   185	    (aX bX aZ bZ uα vα uβ vβ : K)
   186	    (f g : Fin (c + 1) → K) : Polynomial K :=
   187	  (Polynomial.C uα + Polynomial.C vα * Polynomial.X) *
   188	      (linePolynomialOfCoefficients f).comp
   189	        (Polynomial.C aX + Polynomial.C bX * Polynomial.X) +
   190	    (Polynomial.C uβ + Polynomial.C vβ * Polynomial.X) *
   191	      (linePolynomialOfCoefficients g).comp
   192	        (Polynomial.C aZ + Polynomial.C bZ * Polynomial.X)
   193	
   194	/-- The polynomial underlying `combineLinePoly` has degree at most `c + 1`.
   195	This is the degree assertion accompanying Equation `eq:combine-lines` in
   196	blueprint
   197	`def:combine-map`, paper
   198	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:984-989`. -/
   199	theorem combineLinePolynomial_natDegree_le {K : Type*} [CommSemiring K] {c : ℕ}
   200	    (aX bX aZ bZ uα vα uβ vβ : K) (f g : Fin (c + 1) → K) :
   201	    (combineLinePolynomial aX bX aZ bZ uα vα uβ vβ f g).natDegree ≤ c + 1 := by
   202	  have affineDegree : ∀ u v : K,
   203	      (Polynomial.C u + Polynomial.C v * Polynomial.X).natDegree ≤ 1 := by
   204	    intro u v
   205	    refine (Polynomial.natDegree_add_le _ _).trans (max_le ?_ ?_)
   206	    · simp [Polynomial.natDegree_C]
   207	    · refine Polynomial.natDegree_mul_le.trans ?_
   208	      rw [Polynomial.natDegree_C]
   209	      simpa using Polynomial.natDegree_X_le (R := K)
   210	  have summandDegree : ∀ (a b u v : K) (h : Fin (c + 1) → K),
   211	      ((Polynomial.C u + Polynomial.C v * Polynomial.X) *
   212	        (linePolynomialOfCoefficients h).comp
   213	          (Polynomial.C a + Polynomial.C b * Polynomial.X)).natDegree ≤ c + 1 := by
   214	    intro a b u v h
   215	    refine Polynomial.natDegree_mul_le.trans ?_
   216	    have hfactor := affineDegree u v
   217	    have hcomp : ((linePolynomialOfCoefficients h).comp
   218	        (Polynomial.C a + Polynomial.C b * Polynomial.X)).natDegree ≤ c := by
   219	      refine Polynomial.natDegree_comp_le.trans ?_
   220	      calc
   221	        (linePolynomialOfCoefficients h).natDegree *
   222	              (Polynomial.C a + Polynomial.C b * Polynomial.X).natDegree ≤ c * 1 :=
   223	          Nat.mul_le_mul (linePolynomialOfCoefficients_natDegree_le h) (affineDegree a b)
   224	        _ = c := by ring
   225	    omega
   226	  exact (Polynomial.natDegree_add_le _ _).trans
   227	    (max_le (summandDegree aX bX uα vα f) (summandDegree aZ bZ uβ vβ g))
   228	
   229	/-- Combine two degree-`c` line polynomials using explicit affine
   230	reparameterizations.  Coefficients through degree `c + 1` are extracted from
   231	the genuine composed polynomial, so the definition has no incompatibility
   232	fallback.
   233	
   234	This is Equation `eq:combine-lines` in blueprint
   235	`def:combine-map`, paper
   236	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:984-989`. -/
   237	noncomputable def combineLinePoly {K : Type*} [CommSemiring K] {c : ℕ}
   238	    (aX bX aZ bZ uα vα uβ vβ : K)
   239	    (f g : Fin (c + 1) → K) : Fin (c + 1 + 1) → K :=
   240	  fun i => (combineLinePolynomial aX bX aZ bZ uα vα uβ vβ f g).coeff i.val
   241	
   242	/-- Compatibility of an extended line with two projected lines and their
   243	explicit affine parameters. These data witness the projection-inclusion
   244	condition preceding Equation `eq:combine-lines`. The theorem
   245	`exists_isCombineLineCompatible_of_projection_mem` in `Combining/LinePolynomial.lean`
   246	constructs them from that condition, including zero directions. Compatibility
   247	alone does not make every coefficient answer a function on a singleton line;
   248	see issue #695. -/
   249	def IsCombineLineCompatible {K : Type*} [Field K] {m : ℕ}
   250	    (u v : Fin (2 * m + 2) → K)
   251	    (uX vX uZ vZ : Fin m → K)
   252	    (aX bX aZ bZ uα vα uβ vβ : K) : Prop :=
   253	  u (alphaVar m) = uα ∧ v (alphaVar m) = vα ∧
   254	    u (betaVar m) = uβ ∧ v (betaVar m) = vβ ∧
   255	    ∀ t : K,
   256	      projX (u + t • v) = uX + (aX + bX * t) • vX ∧
   257	        projZ (u + t • v) = uZ + (aZ + bZ * t) • vZ
   258	
   259	/-- Under explicit line compatibility, `combineLinePoly` satisfies the
   260	advertised line equation and the two projected points have the stated affine
   261	parameters.  This is the specification obligation for Equation
   262	blueprint
   263	`eq:combine-lines`, paper
   264	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:984-989`. -/
   265	theorem combineLinePoly_spec {K : Type*} [Field K] {m c : ℕ}
   266	    (u v : Fin (2 * m + 2) → K) (uX vX uZ vZ : Fin m → K)
   267	    (aX bX aZ bZ uα vα uβ vβ : K) (f g : Fin (c + 1) → K)
   268	    (hcompat : IsCombineLineCompatible u v uX vX uZ vZ
   269	      aX bX aZ bZ uα vα uβ vβ) :
   270	    ∀ t : K,
   271	      projX (u + t • v) = uX + (aX + bX * t) • vX ∧
   272	      projZ (u + t • v) = uZ + (aZ + bZ * t) • vZ ∧
   273	      evalCoefficient
   274	          (combineLinePoly aX bX aZ bZ uα vα uβ vβ f g) t =
   275	        (uα + t * vα) * evalCoefficient f (aX + bX * t) +
   276	          (uβ + t * vβ) * evalCoefficient g (aZ + bZ * t) := by
   277	  intro t
   278	  obtain ⟨-, -, -, -, hlines⟩ := hcompat
   279	  refine ⟨(hlines t).1, (hlines t).2, ?_⟩
   280	  have hdeg := combineLinePolynomial_natDegree_le aX bX aZ bZ uα vα uβ vβ f g
   281	  have heval :
   282	      evalCoefficient (combineLinePoly aX bX aZ bZ uα vα uβ vβ f g) t =
   283	        (combineLinePolynomial aX bX aZ bZ uα vα uβ vβ f g).eval t := by
   284	    rw [Polynomial.eval_eq_sum_range' (n := c + 1 + 1) (by omega) t]
   285	    simp only [evalCoefficient, combineLinePoly]
   286	    exact Fin.sum_univ_eq_sum_range
   287	      (fun k =>
   288	        (combineLinePolynomial aX bX aZ bZ uα vα uβ vβ f g).coeff k * t ^ k)
   289	      (c + 1 + 1)
   290	  rw [heval, combineLinePolynomial]
   291	  simp only [Polynomial.eval_add, Polynomial.eval_mul, Polynomial.eval_C,
   292	    Polynomial.eval_X, Polynomial.eval_comp, linePolynomialOfCoefficients_eval]
   293	  ring

     4	/-!
     5	# Coordinate blocks of an extended point and of an extended direct sample
     6	
     7	This module records the block decomposition used by the sampling procedure of
     8	the sub-line lemma on the extended dimension.  A point of the extended space
     9	is the tuple consisting of its two source point blocks and its two scalar
    10	coordinates, and this decomposition is a bijection carrying the uniform law to
    11	the uniform law; in particular the two source blocks of a uniform extended
    12	point are independent and uniform.  The decomposition is linear, so it
    13	commutes with the affine parameterization of a line, and it commutes with the
    14	canonical identification of the extended scalar field with the source scalar
    15	field.  The stored coordinate index of an extended direct sample splits along
    16	the same three coordinate ranges.
    17	
    18	## References
    19	
    20	The decompositions support `lem:qld-sublines` in
    21	blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`, whose source is
    22	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`.
    23	The coordinate blocks are those of `def:combine-map`, blueprint lines
    24	445--480, paper lines 970--989.
    25	-/
    26	
    27	open scoped BigOperators
    28	
    29	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    30	
    31	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    32	
    33	noncomputable section
    34	
    35	/-! ## Linearity of the coordinate blocks -/
    36	
    37	/-- The `X` block of a sum of extended points is the sum of the blocks.
    38	Blueprint `def:combine-map`, paper
    39	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:970-989`. -/
    40	theorem projX_add {K : Type*} [AddCommMonoid K] {m : ℕ}
    41	    (u v : Fin (2 * m + 2) → K) :
    42	    projX (u + v) = projX u + projX v := rfl
    43	
    44	/-- The `Z` block of a sum of extended points is the sum of the blocks.
    45	Blueprint `def:combine-map`, paper
    46	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:970-989`. -/
    47	theorem projZ_add {K : Type*} [AddCommMonoid K] {m : ℕ}
    48	    (u v : Fin (2 * m + 2) → K) :
    49	    projZ (u + v) = projZ u + projZ v := rfl
    50	
    51	/-- The `X` block of a scalar multiple of an extended point is the scalar
    52	multiple of the block.  Blueprint `def:combine-map`, paper
    53	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:970-989`. -/
    54	theorem projX_smul {K : Type*} [Monoid K] {m : ℕ} (t : K)
    55	    (u : Fin (2 * m + 2) → K) :
    56	    projX (t • u) = t • projX u := rfl
    57	
    58	/-- The `Z` block of a scalar multiple of an extended point is the scalar
    59	multiple of the block.  Blueprint `def:combine-map`, paper
    60	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:970-989`. -/
    61	theorem projZ_smul {K : Type*} [Monoid K] {m : ℕ} (t : K)
    62	    (u : Fin (2 * m + 2) → K) :
    63	    projZ (t • u) = t • projZ u := rfl
    64	
    65	/-! ## The coordinate blocks of an extended point -/
    66	
    67	/-- Split an extended point into its two source point blocks and its two
    68	scalar coordinates.  Blueprint `def:combine-map`, paper
    69	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:970-989`. -/
    70	def extendedPointBlockEquiv (P : AdmissibleParams) :
    71	    (Fin (2 * P.m + 2) → DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd) ≃
    72	      ((Fin P.m → DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd) ×
    73	          (Fin P.m → DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd)) ×
    74	        (Fin 2 → DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd) :=
    75	  (Equiv.arrowCongr (finCombineEquiv P.m)
    76	      (Equiv.refl (DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd))).trans
    77	    ((Equiv.sumArrowEquivProdArrow _ _ _).trans
    78	      (Equiv.prodCongr (Equiv.sumArrowEquivProdArrow _ _ _) (Equiv.refl _)))
    79	
    80	/-- The first block of the decomposition is the `X` block. -/
    81	theorem extendedPointBlockEquiv_projX (P : AdmissibleParams)
    82	    (u : Fin (2 * P.m + 2) → DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd) :
    83	    (extendedPointBlockEquiv P u).1.1 = projX u := by
    84	  funext i
    85	  rfl
    86	
    87	/-- The second block of the decomposition is the `Z` block. -/
    88	theorem extendedPointBlockEquiv_projZ (P : AdmissibleParams)
    89	    (u : Fin (2 * P.m + 2) → DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd) :
    90	    (extendedPointBlockEquiv P u).1.2 = projZ u := by
    91	  funext i
    92	  rfl
    93	
    94	/-- The first scalar coordinate of the decomposition is `alpha`. -/
    95	theorem extendedPointBlockEquiv_alpha (P : AdmissibleParams)
    96	    (u : Fin (2 * P.m + 2) → DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd) :
    97	    (extendedPointBlockEquiv P u).2 0 = u (alphaVar P.m) := rfl
    98	
    99	/-- The second scalar coordinate of the decomposition is `beta`. -/
   100	theorem extendedPointBlockEquiv_beta (P : AdmissibleParams)
   101	    (u : Fin (2 * P.m + 2) → DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd) :
   102	    (extendedPointBlockEquiv P u).2 1 = u (betaVar P.m) := rfl
   103	
   104	/-- The block decomposition of an extended point carries the uniform law to
   105	the uniform law.  Blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`, paper
   106	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
   107	theorem uniformDistribution_map_extendedPointBlockEquiv (P : AdmissibleParams) :
   108	    (uniformDistribution
   109	          (Fin (2 * P.m + 2) → DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd)).map
   110	        (extendedPointBlockEquiv P) =
   111	      uniformDistribution
   112	        (((Fin P.m → DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd) ×
   113	            (Fin P.m → DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd)) ×
   114	          (Fin 2 → DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd)) :=
   115	  uniformDistribution_map_equiv _
   116	
   117	/-- The two source blocks of a uniformly sampled extended point are
   118	independent and uniform.  Blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`, paper
   119	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
   120	theorem uniformDistribution_map_projX_projZ (P : AdmissibleParams) :
   121	    (uniformDistribution
   122	          (Fin (2 * P.m + 2) → DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd)).map
   123	        (fun u => (projX u, projZ u)) =
   124	      Distribution.prod
   125	        (uniformDistribution (Fin P.m → DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd))
   126	        (uniformDistribution (Fin P.m → DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd)) := by
   127	  have hfun :
   128	      (fun u : Fin (2 * P.m + 2) → DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd =>
   129	          (projX u, projZ u)) =
   130	        fun u => (extendedPointBlockEquiv P u).1 := by
   131	    funext u
   132	    rw [Prod.ext_iff]
   133	    exact ⟨(extendedPointBlockEquiv_projX P u).symm,
   134	      (extendedPointBlockEquiv_projZ P u).symm⟩
   135	  rw [hfun, ← Distribution.map_map _ (extendedPointBlockEquiv P) Prod.fst,
   136	    uniformDistribution_map_extendedPointBlockEquiv,
   137	    uniformDistribution_map_fst, uniformDistribution_prod]
   138	
   139	/-! ## Transport to the source scalar field -/
   140	
   141	/-- The `X` block of an extended point transported to the source scalar field
   142	is the transport of its `X` block.  Blueprint
   143	`def:combine-map`, paper
   144	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:970-989`. -/
   145	theorem projX_directPointToPauli (P : AdmissibleParams)
   146	    (u : Fin P.extendedDirectLd.m → DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd) :
   147	    projX (directPointToPauli P u) =
   148	      fun i => extendedDirectScalarEquiv P (projX u i) := rfl
   149	
   150	/-- The `Z` block of an extended point transported to the source scalar field
   151	is the transport of its `Z` block.  Blueprint
   152	`def:combine-map`, paper
   153	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:970-989`. -/
   154	theorem projZ_directPointToPauli (P : AdmissibleParams)
   155	    (u : Fin P.extendedDirectLd.m → DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd) :
   156	    projZ (directPointToPauli P u) =
   157	      fun i => extendedDirectScalarEquiv P (projZ u i) := rfl
   158	
   159	/-! ## The blocks of an extended direct sample -/
   160	
   161	/-- The stored index, point block and direction block of a uniformly sampled
   162	direct low-degree vector are independent and uniform.  Blueprint
   163	`lem:qld-sublines`, paper
   164	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
   165	theorem uniformDistribution_map_directLdSpaceIndexEquiv (D : DirectLdParams) :
   166	    (uniformDistribution (DirectLdSpace D)).map (directLdSpaceIndexEquiv D) =
   167	      uniformDistribution
   168	        (Fin D.m ×
   169	          ((Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) × (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D))) :=
   170	  uniformDistribution_map_equiv _
   171	
   172	/-! ## Compatibility data read off the coordinate blocks -/
   173	
   174	/-- An extended line is compatible with two source lines as soon as each of
   175	its two point blocks is an affine reparameterization of the corresponding
   176	source line: the base block is a point of the source line and the direction
   177	block is a multiple of the source direction.  The two scalar coordinates of
   178	the compatibility data are the `alpha` and `beta` coordinates of the extended
   179	base and direction.  This supplies the domain condition preceding Equation
   180	`eq:combine-lines` in blueprint
   181	`def:combine-map`, paper
   182	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:970-989`. -/
   183	theorem isCombineLineCompatible_of_blocks {K : Type*} [Field K] {m : ℕ}
   184	    (u v : Fin (2 * m + 2) → K) (uX vX uZ vZ : Fin m → K) (aX bX aZ bZ : K)
   185	    (hX : projX u = uX + aX • vX) (hXv : projX v = bX • vX)
   186	    (hZ : projZ u = uZ + aZ • vZ) (hZv : projZ v = bZ • vZ) :
   187	    IsCombineLineCompatible u v uX vX uZ vZ aX bX aZ bZ
   188	      (u (alphaVar m)) (v (alphaVar m)) (u (betaVar m)) (v (betaVar m)) := by
   189	  refine ⟨rfl, rfl, rfl, rfl, fun t => ⟨?_, ?_⟩⟩
   190	  · rw [projX_add, projX_smul, hX, hXv]
   191	    module
   192	  · rw [projZ_add, projZ_smul, hZ, hZv]
   193	    module
   194	
   195	/-- An extended line whose two source lines carry the inherited direction
   196	blocks is compatible with them, with both affine reparameterizations the
   197	identity.  Blueprint `def:combine-map`, paper
   198	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:970-989`. -/
   199	theorem isCombineLineCompatible_inherited {K : Type*} [Field K] {m : ℕ}
   200	    (u v : Fin (2 * m + 2) → K) :
   201	    IsCombineLineCompatible u v (projX u) (projX v) (projZ u) (projZ v)
   202	      0 1 0 1 (u (alphaVar m)) (v (alphaVar m)) (u (betaVar m))
   203	      (v (betaVar m)) :=
   204	  isCombineLineCompatible_of_blocks u v _ _ _ _ 0 1 0 1
   205	    (by module) (by module) (by module) (by module)

     5	
     6	This module supplies the coefficient evaluation and polynomial representation
     7	shared by the low-degree games and the combining argument. Distinct bounded
     8	coefficient vectors agree at no more parameters than their degree bound.
     9	
    10	## References
    11	
    12	- Blueprint `def:ld-win-predicate` and `lem:coefficient-polynomial-agreement`.
    13	- `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:331-344`.
    14	- `references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:950-955`.
    15

    22	open scoped BigOperators
    23	
    24	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    25	
    26	/-- Evaluation of a coefficient tuple at a field element. This is the
    27	representative convention used by the line answers in blueprint
    28	`def:ld-win-predicate`, paper origin
    29	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
    30	-/
    31	def evalCoefficient {K : Type*} [Semiring K] {n : ℕ}
    32	    (c : Fin n → K) (t : K) : K :=
    33	  ∑ i : Fin n, c i * t ^ i.val
    34	
    35	/-- The polynomial determined by a coefficient tuple evaluates at `param` to
    36	the finite power sum of `coeffs i * param ^ i.val` over `i : Fin size`.
    37	This formalization-only identity connects the coefficient
    38	convention to the root bound used at paper
    39	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:955`. -/
    40	theorem polynomial_ofFn_eval_eq_evalCoefficient {K : Type*} [CommSemiring K]
    41	    [DecidableEq K] {size : ℕ} (coeffs : Fin size -> K) (param : K) :
    42	    (Polynomial.ofFn size coeffs).eval param = evalCoefficient coeffs param := by
    43	  simp [Polynomial.ofFn_eq_sum_monomial, Polynomial.eval_finsetSum,
    44	    Polynomial.eval_monomial, evalCoefficient]
    45	
    46	/-- The univariate polynomial `sum_{i = 0}^c f_i X^i` determined by a bounded
    47	coefficient list. -/
    48	noncomputable def linePolynomialOfCoefficients {K : Type*} [Semiring K]
    49	    {c : ℕ} (f : Fin (c + 1) → K) : Polynomial K :=
    50	  ∑ i : Fin (c + 1), Polynomial.C (f i) * Polynomial.X ^ i.val
    51	
    52	/-- Evaluating the polynomial represented by a coefficient list agrees with
    53	`evalCoefficient`. -/
    54	theorem linePolynomialOfCoefficients_eval {K : Type*} [Semiring K]
    55	    {c : ℕ} (f : Fin (c + 1) → K) (t : K) :
    56	    (linePolynomialOfCoefficients f).eval t = evalCoefficient f t := by
    57	  change Polynomial.eval t
    58	      (∑ i ∈ Finset.univ, Polynomial.C (f i) * Polynomial.X ^ i.val) =
    59	    ∑ i ∈ Finset.univ, f i * t ^ i.val
    60	  rw [Polynomial.eval_finsetSum]
    61	  simp
    62	
    63	/-- The coefficient sum is the polynomial with coefficient `f i` in degree
    64	`i.val` for `i : Fin (c + 1)` and zero coefficients in degrees greater than `c`. -/
    65	theorem linePolynomialOfCoefficients_eq_ofFn {K : Type*} [Semiring K]
    66	    [DecidableEq K] {c : ℕ} (f : Fin (c + 1) → K) :
    67	    linePolynomialOfCoefficients f = Polynomial.ofFn (c + 1) f := by
    68	  simp only [linePolynomialOfCoefficients, Polynomial.ofFn_eq_sum_monomial,
    69	    Polynomial.C_mul_X_pow_eq_monomial]
    70	
    71	/-- Distinct bounded coefficient vectors represent distinct polynomials. -/
    72	theorem linePolynomialOfCoefficients_injective {K : Type*} [Semiring K] (c : ℕ) :
    73	    Function.Injective (linePolynomialOfCoefficients (K := K) (c := c)) := by
    74	  classical
    75	  intro first second heq
    76	  exact Polynomial.injective_ofFn (c + 1)
    77	    (by simpa only [linePolynomialOfCoefficients_eq_ofFn] using heq)
    78	
    79	/-- The polynomial of a bounded coefficient vector has degree at most `n`. -/
    80	theorem linePolynomialOfCoefficients_natDegree_le {K : Type*} [Semiring K] {n : ℕ}
    81	    (f : Fin (n + 1) → K) :
    82	    (linePolynomialOfCoefficients f).natDegree ≤ n := by
    83	  classical
    84	  rw [linePolynomialOfCoefficients_eq_ofFn]
    85	  exact Nat.lt_succ_iff.mp (Polynomial.ofFn_natDegree_lt (Nat.succ_pos n) f)
    86

    88	more than `bound` elements of a finite integral domain. This is the univariate
    89	root bound underlying the Schwartz-Zippel step in `lem:qld-xz-lines`, paper
    90	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:955`.

    24	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT

    26	open scoped BigOperators

    28	variable {K : Type*} [Field K]
    29	
    30	/--
    31	The affine line through `u` in direction `v`, including the singleton case
    32	`v = 0`.  Blueprint `def:line`; paper origin
    33	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:106-124`.
    34	-/
    35	def linePoints {m : ℕ}
    36	    (u v : Fin m → K) : Set (Fin m → K) :=
    37	  {x | ∃ t : K, x = u + t • v}
    38	
    39	/-- The elementary coordinate direction used in the axis-parallel predicate of
    40	blueprint `def:line`; paper origin
    41	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:106-124`.
    42	-/
    43	def coordinateDirection {m : ℕ}
    44	    (i : Fin m) : Fin m → K :=
    45	  Pi.single i 1
    46	
    47	/--
    48	`IsAxisParallel v` means that `v` is a standard coordinate direction.  This is
    49	the axis-parallel clause of blueprint `def:line` (paper
    50	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:106-124`).
    51	-/
    52	def IsAxisParallel {m : ℕ} (v : Fin m → K) : Prop :=
    53	  ∃ i : Fin m, v = coordinateDirection i
    54	
    55	/--
    56	The diagonal-direction predicate from blueprint `def:line`; a prefix of coordinates may
    57	vanish.  Paper origin
    58	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:106-124`.
    59	-/
    60	def IsDiagonal {m : ℕ} (v : Fin m → K) : Prop :=
    61	  ∃ i : Fin m, ∀ j : Fin m, j.1 < i.1 → v j = 0
    62	
    63	/--
    64	Changing the base point to another point on a line leaves the line unchanged.
    65	This is blueprint `prop:line-equiv`,
    66	with paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:128-132`.
    67	-/
    68	theorem linePoints_eq_of_mem {m : ℕ}
    69	    (u v u' : Fin m → K) (h : u' ∈ linePoints u v) :
    70	    linePoints u v = linePoints u' v := by
    71	  obtain ⟨t, rfl⟩ := h
    72	  ext x
    73	  constructor
    74	  · rintro ⟨s, rfl⟩
    75	    exact ⟨s - t, by module⟩
    76	  · rintro ⟨s, rfl⟩
    77	    exact ⟨t + s, by module⟩
    78	
    79	/--
    80	The canonical linear representative map of a line direction.  It projects onto
    81	the coordinate complement of the span of `v`; for `v = 0` the span is bottom,
    82	so the resulting map is the identity.  Blueprint `def:line-representative`;
    83	paper origin
    84	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:143-174`.
    85	-/
    86	noncomputable def lineRepMap {m : ℕ}
    87	    (v : Fin m → K) : (Fin m → K) →ₗ[K] (Fin m → K) :=
    88	  canonicalProjOfKernel (Submodule.span K ({v} : Set (Fin m → K)))

\section{Key theorem forms}

Let $\widehat\psi$ be the normalized expanded state of a projective strategy
winning the Pauli basis test with probability at least $1-\eps$. Write
$L^W_f(\ell)$ and $M^W_a(u)$ for its expanded line and point effects. For
the subline law $D$, abbreviate the two correlations by
\begin{align*}
 A(T)&=\E_D\E_{(x,z,\alpha,\beta)\in\ell}
   \sum_{f_X,f_Z}\langle\widehat\psi,
   (T^{\ell_X,\ell_Z}_{f_X,f_Z}\ot
     M^Z_{f_Z(z)}(z)M^X_{f_X(x)}(x))\widehat\psi\rangle,\\
 B(T)&=\E_D\E_{(x,z,\alpha,\beta)\in\ell}
   \sum_{f_X,f_Z}\langle\widehat\psi,
   (T^{\ell_X,\ell_Z}_{f_X,f_Z}\ot
     M^Z_{f_Z(z)}(z))\widehat\psi\rangle.
\end{align*}
The paper's Claim 17-2 states
\[
 |A(T)-B(T)|\leq O\bigl(m\sqrt{\delta_{\mathrm{Line}}(\eps)}\bigr)
 \quad\text{for}\quad
 T^{\ell_X,\ell_Z}_{f_X,f_Z}
 =L^X_{f_X}(\ell_X)L^Z_{f_Z}(\ell_Z)L^X_{f_X}(\ell_X).
\]
Let $A_{\rm dir}$ and $B_{\rm dir}$ denote the same expressions for the
auxiliary subline law whose coordinate indices are sampled uniformly and
directly, with completed evaluations. The established Lean result is
\[
 |\operatorname{Re}A_{\rm dir}(T)-\operatorname{Re}B_{\rm dir}(T)|
 \le C m\sqrt{\delta_{\mathrm{Line}}(\eps)},
\]
for a universal $C>0$, the concrete sandwich above, and every directly
indexed subline witness. It assumes no joint-point or paired-line
consistency witness. This is not yet the complex estimate on the source law.
The former Lean declaration quantified instead over every paired-line POVM
with the degree support and evaluated consistency conclusions of the
combined-lines lemma. Its scalar errors $\delta_P,\delta_Q$ were arbitrary,
independently of $\eps$. The right-hand side remained the same, with
$\delta_{\mathrm{Line}}(\eps)=\sqrt\eps$.

\section{The construction used by the source}

The paired-line measurement is defined by the displayed sandwich in the
proof of the combined-lines lemma. Claim 17-2 uses this definition to sum
over the Z polynomial:
\[
 \sum_{f_Z}T^{\ell_X,\ell_Z}_{f_X,f_Z}
 =L^X_{f_X}(\ell_X)
   \Bigl(\sum_{f_Z}L^Z_{f_Z}(\ell_Z)\Bigr)L^X_{f_X}(\ell_X)
 =L^X_{f_X}(\ell_X).
\]
The last equality uses completeness and projectivity. Cauchy--Schwarz
reduces the scalar difference to the square root of the resulting
X-line/point consistency deficit. The separate X marginal of the subline
law is sufficient; no joint conditional law for $(x,z)$ is needed.
Restriction to a line kind and coordinate costs a factor $2m$, so the
resulting square-root estimate is bounded by the paper's stated error
because $m\geq1$.\footnote{The construction is at lines 942--949 and the

\section{A counterexample to the enlarged domain}

Choose an admissible tuple with $q>1$ and a perfect projective strategy.
The honest strategy in the completeness lemma supplies one; for example,
$(q,m,d)=(8,1,1)$ is admissible. Its expanded state has norm one. For
$a\in\F_q$, let $c_a$ be the constant polynomial with value $a$. For both
players and every line pair, define a POVM by
\[
 T_{c_a,c_b}=q^{-2}I\quad(a,b\in\F_q),\qquad
 T_{f_X,f_Z}=0\quad\text{for every other pair}.
\]
There are $q^2$ nonzero effects, so they sum to $I$. Both axis-degree
requirements hold. At any incident point a constant polynomial has a
uniquely determined value, even on a zero-direction line. Thus the optional
evaluation in Lean returns the ordinary field value, never an undefined
outcome, for every nonzero effect in this example.

The evaluated POVM is uniform on the $q^2$ point pairs. Against any complete
joint point measurement $Q$, its agreement is $q^{-2}$ and its consistency
defect is $1-q^{-2}$. Therefore the line-witness requirements hold with
$\delta_P=1$ in every opposite placement. A point witness also exists within
the former public domain: take the projective measurement which always
answers $(0,0)$. It is exactly self-consistent and has both ordered-product
distances at most $4$. Indeed, the squared norms of either ordered product
family sum to one, by projectivity and completeness, and
\begin{align*}
 \sum_{a,b}\|(Q_{a,b}-M^X_aM^Z_b)\widehat\psi\|^2
 &\leq 2\sum_{a,b}\|Q_{a,b}\widehat\psi\|^2\\
 &\quad+2\sum_{a,b}\|M^X_aM^Z_b\widehat\psi\|^2\\
 &=4.
\end{align*}
The reversed ordering satisfies the same calculation. Hence $\delta_Q=4$
is allowed by every point-witness field. These constants are permitted by
the former scalar quantifiers; the argument does not require them to be
polynomially small functions of $\eps$.

For each supported subline sample, completeness gives
\[
 A(T)=q^{-2}\sum_{a,b}\langle\widehat\psi,
    (I\ot M^Z_bM^X_a)\widehat\psi\rangle=q^{-2},
 \qquad
 B(T)=q^{-2}\sum_{a,b}\langle\widehat\psi,
    (I\ot M^Z_b)\widehat\psi\rangle=q^{-1}.
\]
The first equality uses $\sum_bM^Z_b\sum_aM^X_a=I$, without a commutation
assumption. Probability averaging preserves these constants. The absolute
difference is therefore $(q-1)/q^2>0$, whereas the claimed bound is zero at
$\eps=0$. For $q=8$ the difference is $7/64$. The same perfect strategy is
admissible at arbitrarily small positive $\eps$, so excluding zero or
enlarging a universal constant cannot repair the claim. No polynomially
vanishing error depending on $\eps$ alone absorbs this difference.
